# sigma_api_credential (Resource)

Creates an OAuth2 client_id / client_secret pair for the Sigma REST API.

**⚠ Use an encrypted Terraform state backend.** This resource stores `client_secret` in state because Sigma's API returns the secret only once at create time and provides no GET endpoint to retrieve it later. Local-disk state is unsuitable for this resource — use S3 + KMS, Terraform Cloud / Enterprise, HashiCorp Vault, or another encrypted remote backend. Losing or exposing the state means rotating the credential.

Any change to inputs forces replacement (Sigma has no PATCH for credentials).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sigma_api_credential" "ci" {
  owner_id    = sigma_member.alice.id
  name        = "ci-pipeline"
  description = "Used by the CI pipeline to apply Terraform changes."
  scopes      = ["api"]
}

# The secret is only available at create time. Surface it to a downstream
# consumer (a vault, AWS Secrets Manager, etc.) within the same apply.
output "ci_client_id" {
  value = sigma_api_credential.ci.client_id
}

output "ci_client_secret" {
  value     = sigma_api_credential.ci.client_secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String)
- `owner_id` (String) Member UUID that will own the credential.

### Optional

- `description` (String)
- `scopes` (Set of String) One or more of `api`, `embed`. Defaults to `[api]`. Changing this forces replacement (rotates the credential).

### Read-Only

- `client_id` (String)
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) Returned ONCE at create. Never re-readable. Surfaced to state and may be referenced via `nonsensitive(...)` only when intentional.
- `id` (String) Equal to client_id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Sigma never returns client_secret, so it is empty after import.
# Recreate the credential if you need a usable secret in state.
terraform import sigma_api_credential.example '<client_id>'
```
